reviewType: Independent read-only source review and inspection of pre-existing parent development stdout/results. No tests, pure probes, MCP/native/helper execution, GUI, build or source edits by reviewer in this integration round.
scope: Product execution_receipt integration with graph/private-blob validation, stricter Node metadata probe acceptance, strict archived journal JSON decoding, and the changed real-stdio/unit qualification sources.
scopeSeparation: Earlier context and pure-validator/preparation freezes retain their historical scopes. This source snapshot contains acknowledged drift and does not inherit runtime acceptance from those earlier frozen inputs.
outcome: No new actionable source finding identified within this reader-integration slice.
sourceChecks: Product execution_receipt now calls read_validated_receipts; returned semantic_validation is produced only after graph and every referenced private argument/native frame blob are validated.

ExecutionJournalError from semantic/private-blob validation returns explicit ok=false, typed code, outcome=unknown, incomplete=true and request_terminal_observed=false. That branch does not expose raw records, private blob contents, semantic success or metadata_probe.

The probe result is computed from real SDK metadata, but is attached only to the successful validated-reader return. A failed blob validation cannot return a positive probe ACK through the ordinary typed error branch.

Node safe probe requires ok===true and semantic_validation.semantic_version===1 in addition to nonce, expected SDK numeric fingerprint, codec and worker identity checks. Unit counterexamples cover explicit failed reader and missing semantic reader capability.

Journal marker and event decoding now rejects duplicate object keys at any depth, NaN/Infinity and floating exponent overflow. Published hash validity alone cannot cause the last duplicate ok field to become an authoritative terminal.

Ambiguous event JSON is handled as a bounded valid prefix with incomplete=true. It can remain a successful read operation while lifecycle completeness remains unknown; read success is not execution success or replay safety.

Graph lifecycle completeness and reported terminal outcomes stay separate. Root/handler terminal and lifecycle_unknown=false do not establish application consumption, absence of side effects or replay_safe.
No write-protocol, metadata authority or normal well-formed trace semantics were changed by the strict JSON reader addition.

existingParentDevelopmentEvidence.scope: Parent real MCP stdio run used wait and mouse-position read-only queries. Corrupt private blob and ambiguous archive writes were confined to the isolated fixture; no held-state or posted-input scenario was exercised.

fixtureRetentionClarification: The test immediately verifies that failed reader validation does not rewrite/reset the corrupted private blob. A successful harness run then removes its entire isolated root, and context-v7 results records retained=false. Thus preservation is a reader nonmutation assertion at validation time, not an archival guarantee that the original corrupted blob remains after successful fixture cleanup. Raw stdout and results.json are separately retained.
